chapters.title: Hilhot Rechilut and Ezehu Rechil
chapters.about: passing gossip between people and bringing a third person into a rebuke

chapters.title: Passing True Information
chapters.about: creating hatred between friends even when speaking total truth

chapters.title: Demands from a Father, Rabbi, or Boss
chapters.about: refusing to speak gossip even if facing loss of livelihood

chapters.title: Ne'elavim Ve'enan Olvim
chapters.about: remaining silent when put down and the creation of the sun and moon

chapters.title: Answering Questions and Lying for Shalom
chapters.about: how to answer when asked what someone said about them

chapters.title: Gemara Sanhedrin on Bet Din Decisions
chapters.about: how judges write a decision without identifying who voted to obligate

summary: Rabbi Soffer speaks about Hilhot Rechilut from the Hafez Chaim, explaining the case of passing information between people even when it is true. He discusses handling situations where a boss, father, or Rabbi asks for details, as well as the reward for remaining silent when put down. He also reviews Gemara Sanhedrin regarding how a Bet Din records a decision and Gemara Ketubot regarding dancing before a Kala to preserve shalom.
subjects: Refusing a boss who demands gossip
Creation of the sun and moon in Beresheet
Gemara Sanhedrin on recording a Bet Din decision
Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel in Ketubot
questions: What defines a person who is called a Rakhil?
Is one allowed to speak Rechilut if a boss threatens to fire them?
What is the spiritual reward for someone who hears put-downs and stays silent?
How does a Bet Din write a decision without creating hatred between parties?
When is a person permitted to say something untrue for the purpose of shalom?
